docs.title: PM (PromptManager)
docs.text: "Prompts with superpowers" Parse YAML metadata from markdown, expand shell references, and render ERB templates on demand PM (PromptManager) treats prompt files as composable, parameterized templates. Write prompts in markdown with YAML front matter, shell references, and ERB — PM handles the rest.  Key Features <li> YAML Metadata - Parse from markdown strings or files <li> Shell Expansion - $VAR, ${VAR}, and $(command) substitution <li> ERB Rendering - On-demand rendering with named parameters <li> File Includes - Compose prompts from multiple files <li> Custom Directives - Register custom methods for ERB templates <li> Configurable Pipeline - Enable/disable stages per prompt or globally <li> Comment Stripping - HTML comments removed before processing

docs.title: Processing Pipeline
docs.text:
Every prompt passes through four stages:

graph LR
    A[Strip HTML Comments] --> B[Extract YAML Metadata]
    B --> C[Shell Expansion]
    C --> D["ERB Rendering (on to_s)"]
  1. Strip HTML comments -- <!-- ... --> removed before anything else
  2. Extract YAML metadata -- Front-matter between --- fences parsed into PM::Metadata
  3. Shell expansion -- Environment variables and commands expanded (when shell: true)
  4. ERB rendering -- Templates evaluated on demand when to_s is called (when erb: true)

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
Given a file review.md:

---
title: Code Review
parameters:
  language: ruby
  code: null
---
Review the following <%= language %> code:

<%= code %>

Parse and render:

require 'pm'

parsed = PM.parse('review.md')
puts parsed.metadata.title        #=> "Code Review"
puts parsed.to_s('code' => source) #=> rendered prompt

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Default Description prompts_dir String '' Prepended to relative file paths in PM.parse shell Boolean true Default shell expansion setting for new parses erb Boolean true Default ERB rendering setting for new parses

All attributes have both getter and setter methods (attr_accessor).

docs.title: initialize
docs.text: Creates a new Configuration with default values by calling reset!.

docs.title: reset! → nil
docs.text:
Restores all attributes to their defaults:

PM.config.reset!

PM.config.prompts_dir  #=> ''
PM.config.shell        #=> true
PM.config.erb          #=> true

docs.title: Block Configuration
docs.text:
PM.configure do |config|
  config.prompts_dir = '~/.prompts'
  config.shell = false
end

docs.title: Direct Access
docs.text:
PM.config.prompts_dir = '/usr/share/prompts'
PM.config.erb = false

docs.title: Override Behavior
docs.text:
Per-file YAML metadata always overrides the global setting. If a file has shell: true in its front-matter, shell expansion runs even when PM.config.shell is false.

The global setting acts as the default when a file does not specify the value.

Current version of the PM library. Defined in lib/pm/version.rb.

docs.title: PM::METADATA_REGEXP
docs.text:
PM::METADATA_REGEXP

Matches YAML front-matter delimited by --- fences. Captures the YAML content between the fences and the remaining body.

Used internally by PM.parse to separate metadata from content.

docs.title: PM::HTML_COMMENT_REGEXP
docs.text:
PM::HTML_COMMENT_REGEXP

Matches HTML comments (<!-- ... -->), including multiline comments. Uses the m (multiline) flag for dot-matches-newline behavior.

Used by PM.strip_comments.

docs.title: PM::ENV_VAR_REGEXP
docs.text:
PM::ENV_VAR_REGEXP

Matches environment variable references in two forms:

  • ${VAR} -- braced form (captured in group 1)
  • $VAR -- bare form (captured in group 2)

Only matches UPPERCASE variable names ([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*). Lowercase names are intentionally ignored to avoid conflicts with ERB and other syntax.

Used by PM.expand_shell during the environment variable expansion phase.

docs.title: PM::COMMAND_START
docs.text:
PM::COMMAND_START  #=> "$("

String marker that identifies the start of a command substitution. Used by the shell expansion parser to find $(command) sequences with proper handling of nested parentheses.

docs.title: PM::Metadata
docs.text: OpenStruct-based metadata container with automatic predicate methods for boolean values.

docs.title: Source
docs.text: lib/pm/metadata.rb

docs.title: Inheritance
docs.text:
OpenStruct
  └── PM::Metadata

docs.title: Metadata.new(hash = {}) → Metadata
docs.text:
Creates a new metadata object. All hash keys become accessible via dot notation. Boolean values also get predicate methods.

meta = PM::Metadata.new(title: 'Hello', shell: true, erb: false)

meta.title   #=> "Hello"
meta.shell   #=> true
meta.shell?  #=> true
meta.erb     #=> false
meta.erb?    #=> false

docs.title: Dot Notation Access
docs.text:
All YAML keys from the front-matter are accessible as methods:

parsed = PM.parse("---\ntitle: Test\nprovider: openai\nmodel: gpt-4\n---\nContent")

parsed.metadata.title     #=> "Test"
parsed.metadata.provider  #=> "openai"
parsed.metadata.model     #=> "gpt-4"

docs.title: Predicate Methods
docs.text:
Boolean keys (true or false values) automatically get a ?-suffixed predicate method:

meta = PM::Metadata.new(shell: true, verbose: false)

meta.shell?    #=> true
meta.verbose?  #=> false

Non-boolean keys do not get predicate methods:

meta = PM::Metadata.new(title: 'Test')
meta.respond_to?(:title?)  #=> false

docs.title: File-Specific Keys
docs.text:
When PM.parse reads from a file, these keys are added automatically:

Key Type Description directory String Absolute path to the parent directory name String Filename (e.g., review.md) created_at Time File creation timestamp modified_at Time Last modification timestamp

docs.title: parameters
docs.text:
The parameters hash from YAML front-matter:

parsed.metadata.parameters
#=> {"language" => "ruby", "code" => nil}

Keys with nil values are required parameters. Keys with any other value are defaults.

docs.title: includes
docs.text:
Populated after to_s is called. Contains a tree of included files:

parsed.metadata.includes
#=> [{ path: "/path/to/header.md", depth: 1, metadata: {...}, includes: [] }]

This is nil before to_s and is reset on each to_s call.

docs.title: shell and erb
docs.text: Control processing behavior. Default to true when not specified in the YAML. The global configuration default is applied during metadata construction.

docs.title: PM::Parsed
docs.text: The result object returned by PM.parse. A Struct with two fields: metadata and content.

docs.title: Source
docs.text: lib/pm/parsed.rb

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: PM::Parsed = Struct.new(:metadata, :content)

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description metadata PM::Metadata Parsed YAML front-matter content String Markdown content after metadata extraction and shell expansion

docs.title: [](key) → Object
docs.text:
Bracket accessor that delegates to metadata:

parsed = PM.parse("---\ntitle: Hello\n---\nContent")

parsed[:title]    #=> "Hello"
parsed['title']   #=> "Hello"

docs.title: to_s(values = {}) → String
docs.text:
Render the prompt content with ERB template evaluation.

Parameters:

Name Type Description values Hash Parameter values to merge with defaults

Returns: Rendered prompt as String.

Raises: ArgumentError if required parameters (those with nil defaults) are not provided.

Behavior:

  1. Merges provided values with parameter defaults from metadata
  2. Validates all required parameters are present
  3. If erb: true, evaluates ERB with parameters and registered directives
  4. If erb: false, returns content as-is
  5. Populates metadata.includes with the include tree
parsed = PM.parse('review.md')

# With required params
result = parsed.to_s('code' => File.read('app.rb'))

# Override defaults
result = parsed.to_s('code' => source, 'language' => 'python')

# Symbol keys work
result = parsed.to_s(code: source)

docs.title: render_with(values, included, depth) → String
docs.text:
Internal method used by to_s and the include directive. Handles the ERB rendering pipeline with include tracking.

Parameters:

Name Type Description values Hash Merged parameter values included Set File paths already in the include chain depth Integer Current include nesting depth

This method is not typically called directly.

docs.title: Typical Usage
docs.text:
parsed = PM.parse('prompt.md')

# Access metadata
parsed.metadata.title
parsed.metadata.parameters

# Render
output = parsed.to_s('key' => 'value')

# Check includes after render
parsed.metadata.includes

docs.title: PM Module
docs.text: The top-level PM module is the primary interface. All public methods are class methods on PM.

docs.title: PM.parse(source) → Parsed
docs.text:
Parse a file or string and return a PM::Parsed object.

Parameters:

Name Type Description source String, Symbol, Pathname File path (.md extension or Pathname), Symbol, single word, or raw string

Returns: PM::Parsed (Struct with metadata and content)

Behavior:

  • If source is a Symbol or a single word (letters, digits, underscores only), .md is appended and it is treated as a file basename
  • If source is a Pathname, responds to to_path, or is a String ending in .md, it is treated as a file path
  • File paths are resolved relative to PM.config.prompts_dir (unless absolute)
  • File parsing adds directory, name, created_at, modified_at to metadata
  • Processing pipeline: strip comments → extract YAML → shell expansion
# File
parsed = PM.parse('review.md')

# Symbol or single word (basename — .md appended)
parsed = PM.parse(:review)      #=> parses review.md
parsed = PM.parse('review')     #=> parses review.md

# String
parsed = PM.parse("---\ntitle: Hello\n---\nContent")

docs.title: PM.config → Configuration
docs.text:
Returns the singleton PM::Configuration instance.

PM.config.prompts_dir  #=> ''
PM.config.shell        #=> true

docs.title: PM.configure { |config| } → Configuration
docs.text:
Yields the configuration instance for block-style configuration.

PM.configure do |config|
  config.prompts_dir = '~/.prompts'
  config.shell = true
  config.erb = true
end

docs.title: PM.strip_comments(string) → String
docs.text:
Remove all HTML comments (<!-- ... -->) from the string, including multiline.

PM.strip_comments("Hello <!-- removed --> World")
#=> "Hello  World"

docs.title: PM.expand_shell(string) → String
docs.text:
Expand shell references in the string.

  • $VAR and ${VAR} → environment variable value (empty string if unset)
  • $(command) → command stdout (trailing newline stripped)

Only UPPERCASE variable names are expanded.

PM.expand_shell("User: $USER, Date: $(date +%Y-%m-%d)")
#=> "User: dewayne, Date: 2025-01-15"

Raises: RuntimeError if a command exits with non-zero status.

docs.title: PM.register(*names, &block) → nil
docs.text:
Register one or more named directives available in ERB templates. Multiple names register the same block under each name (aliases).

Parameters:

Name Type Description *names Symbols, Strings One or more directive names block Proc Receives RenderContext as first arg, then user args

Raises: RuntimeError if any name is already registered.

PM.register(:env) { |_ctx, key| ENV.fetch(key, '') }
PM.register(:webpage, :website, :web) { |_ctx, url| fetch_page(url) }

docs.title: PM.directives → Hash
docs.text:
Returns the current directive registry.

PM.directives
#=> { include: #<Proc>, env: #<Proc> }

docs.title: PM.reset_directives! → nil
docs.text:
Remove all custom directives and re-register only the built-in include directive.

PM.reset_directives!
PM.directives.keys  #=> [:include]

docs.title: PM::RenderContext
docs.text: Context object passed as the first argument to every directive block during ERB rendering.

docs.title: Source
docs.text: lib/pm/parsed.rb

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: PM::RenderContext = Struct.new(:directory, :params, :included, :depth, :metadata)

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description directory String Absolute path to the directory of the file being rendered params Hash Merged parameter values (defaults + overrides) included Set File paths already in the include chain (for circular detection) depth Integer Include nesting depth (0 for top-level file) metadata PM::Metadata Metadata of the file being rendered

docs.title: Usage in Directives
docs.text:
Every directive block receives a RenderContext as its first argument:

PM.register(:current_file) { |ctx| ctx.metadata.name || 'unknown' }

PM.register(:nesting) { |ctx| ctx.depth.to_s }

PM.register(:sibling) do |ctx, filename|
  File.read(File.join(ctx.directory, filename))
end

PM.register(:param_dump) do |ctx|
  ctx.params.map { |k, v| "#{k}: #{v}" }.join(', ')
end

docs.title: Context During Includes
docs.text:
When a file is included, the RenderContext reflects the included file's state:

  • directory is the included file's directory
  • metadata is the included file's metadata
  • depth increments by 1 for each nesting level
  • included contains all ancestor file paths
  • params carries the parent's merged parameter values

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Technical details about PM's internal design.

  • Processing Pipeline -- The four-stage pipeline that transforms raw prompts
  • Design Decisions -- Rationale behind key architectural choices

docs.title: Design Decisions
docs.text: Key architectural choices and their rationale.

docs.title: OpenStruct for Metadata
docs.text:
PM::Metadata extends OpenStruct, providing dynamic dot-notation access to any YAML key without predeclaring attributes.

Why: Prompt metadata is inherently schemaless. Different prompts carry different keys (provider, model, temperature, parameters, custom keys). OpenStruct allows any key without configuration.

Trade-off: Slightly slower than a fixed Struct for attribute access, but metadata objects are small and accessed infrequently relative to the parsing work.

docs.title: ERB for Templates
docs.text:
ERB was chosen as the template engine rather than Mustache, Liquid, or a custom syntax.

Why:

  • Ships with Ruby's standard library -- no additional dependencies
  • Familiar to every Ruby developer
  • Full Ruby expressions available (not just variable substitution)
  • Custom directives integrate naturally as method calls

Trade-off: ERB can execute arbitrary Ruby, which is more powerful than needed for simple variable substitution. PM mitigates this by encouraging the use of parameters and directives rather than inline Ruby logic.

docs.title: Parse-Time vs Render-Time Split
docs.text:
Shell expansion runs at parse time. ERB rendering runs on demand at to_s time.

Why:

  • Shell references ($USER, $(date)) represent the environment at the time the prompt is loaded. They should reflect current state when the file is read.
  • ERB parameters represent per-invocation values that may change between calls. Deferring rendering allows the same parsed prompt to be rendered multiple times with different values.

docs.title: Separate Shell and ERB Flags
docs.text:
Both shell and erb can be independently enabled or disabled per file.

Why: Some prompts are documentation templates that should show $VAR syntax literally. Others need shell expansion but contain ERB syntax meant for a different renderer. Independent flags give full control.

docs.title: Include via ERB Directive
docs.text:
File inclusion uses <%= include 'path.md' %> rather than a preprocessor directive or custom syntax.

Why:

  • Consistent with the ERB rendering model -- includes are just another method call
  • Parameters flow naturally from parent to child
  • Custom directives use the same mechanism, so the system is uniform
  • No new syntax to learn

Trade-off: Includes only work when ERB is enabled. Setting erb: false disables includes.

docs.title: Circular Include Detection
docs.text:
PM tracks included file paths in a Set passed through the render chain.

Why: Circular includes would cause infinite recursion. The Set provides O(1) lookup and is threaded through the RenderContext without global state.

docs.title: Configuration as Singleton
docs.text:
PM.config returns a single PM::Configuration instance. Per-file metadata overrides it.

Why: A global default makes sense for project-wide settings like prompts_dir. The override mechanism means individual files always have the final say, avoiding surprises.

docs.title: UPPERCASE-Only Shell Variables
docs.text:
Only $UPPER_CASE variable names are expanded by shell expansion. $lowercase is left as-is.

Why: This avoids conflicts with ERB and other syntaxes that might use $ followed by lowercase characters. Environment variables are conventionally uppercase, so this covers the practical use case without false matches.

docs.title: Processing Pipeline
docs.text: PM processes prompts through a four-stage pipeline. The first three stages run at parse time; the fourth runs on demand when to_s is called.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
graph TD
    A["Raw Input<br/>(file, symbol, word, or string)"] --> B["1. Strip HTML Comments"]
    B --> C["2. Extract YAML Metadata"]
    C --> D["3. Shell Expansion"]
    D --> E["PM::Parsed<br/>(metadata + content)"]
    E -->|"to_s(values)"| F["4. ERB Rendering"]
    F --> G["Rendered String"]

    style A fill:#00695c,color:#fff
    style E fill:#00695c,color:#fff
    style G fill:#f57f17,color:#000

docs.title: Stage 1: Strip HTML Comments
docs.text:
When: Parse time Method: PM.strip_comments

All <!-- ... --> comments are removed, including multiline spans. This runs first so comments don't interfere with metadata extraction.

Input:  "<!-- draft -->
---
title: Test
---
Content <!-- note -->"
Output: "
---
title: Test
---
Content "

docs.title: Stage 2: Extract YAML Metadata
docs.text:
When: Parse time Regex: PM::METADATA_REGEXP

The ----delimited front-matter is parsed with YAML.safe_load into a Hash, then wrapped in a PM::Metadata object. Global defaults for shell and erb are applied if the file doesn't specify them.

For file sources, directory, name, created_at, and modified_at are added from file stats.

Input:  "---
title: Test
shell: true
---
Content"
Output: metadata = PM::Metadata(title: "Test", shell: true, erb: true)
        content  = "Content"

docs.title: Stage 3: Shell Expansion
docs.text:
When: Parse time (if shell: true) Method: PM.expand_shell

Two sub-stages run in order:

docs.title: 3a. Command Substitution
docs.text: $(command) sequences are found (with proper nesting of parentheses), executed, and replaced with stdout.

docs.title: 3b. Environment Variables
docs.text:
$VAR and ${VAR} patterns (UPPERCASE only) are replaced with the corresponding environment variable value. Missing variables become empty strings.

Input:  "User: $USER\nDate: $(date +%Y-%m-%d)"
Output: "User: dewayne\nDate: 2025-01-15"

docs.title: Stage 4: ERB Rendering
docs.text:
When: On demand (to_s call, if erb: true) Method: PM::Parsed#to_s

The content is evaluated as an ERB template. Parameter values (defaults merged with to_s arguments) and registered directives are available as local methods in the template.

This stage also handles the include directive, which recursively parses and renders included files through the full pipeline.

Input:  "Hello, <%= name %>!"  (with params: {name: "Alice"})
Output: "Hello, Alice!"

docs.title: Conditional Stages
docs.text:
Stages 3 and 4 can be independently disabled:

Setting Effect shell: false Stage 3 skipped; $VAR and $(cmd) preserved erb: false Stage 4 skipped; <%= ... %> preserved

Settings can be per-file (YAML metadata) or global (PM.configure). Per-file always wins.

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
graph LR
    subgraph "Parse Time"
        A[Raw Text] --> B[No Comments]
        B --> C[Metadata + Content]
        C --> D[Shell-Expanded Content]
    end

    subgraph "Render Time"
        D --> E[ERB Template]
        E --> F[Final Output]
    end

    style A fill:#00695c,color:#fff
    style F fill:#f57f17,color:#000

The PM::Parsed object returned by PM.parse holds the result of stages 1-3. Calling to_s triggers stage 4 and returns the final string.

docs.title: Prompt Library Structure
docs.text:
Organize prompts by agent role and task:

~/.prompts/
  agents/
    code_assistant/
      system.md
      review.md
      refactor.md
      explain.md
    writer/
      system.md
      draft.md
      edit.md
    analyst/
      system.md
      summarize.md
      compare.md
  common/
    output_json.md
    output_markdown.md
    safety.md

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: PM.configure { |c| c.prompts_dir = '~/.prompts' }

docs.title: System Prompt Pattern
docs.text:
agents/code_assistant/system.md:

---
title: Code Assistant System Prompt
provider: anthropic
model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514
role: system
---
You are an expert software engineer. You help with code review,
refactoring, and explanation.

Current environment:
- OS: $(uname -s)
- User: $USER
- Working directory: $(pwd)

<%= include '../common/safety.md' %>

docs.title: Task Prompts with Parameters
docs.text:
agents/code_assistant/review.md:

---
title: Code Review Task
role: user
parameters:
  code: null
  language: null
  focus: general
---
<%= include '../common/output_markdown.md' %>

Review the following <%= language %> code with a focus on <%= focus %>:

```<%= language %>
<%= code %>

## Custom Directives for Agent Integration

Register directives that fetch context dynamically:

```ruby
PM.register(:git_diff) do |_ctx|
  `git diff --cached`.chomp
end

PM.register(:recent_commits) do |_ctx, count|
  `git log --oneline -#{count}`.chomp
end

PM.register(:file_tree) do |ctx, path|
  dir = path || ctx.directory
  `find #{dir} -type f -name '*.rb' | head -20`.chomp
end

Use them in prompts:

---
title: PR Review
parameters:
  focus: correctness
---
Review this PR with a focus on <%= focus %>.

Changes:
<%= git_diff %>

Recent commit context:
<%= recent_commits 5 %>

Project structure:
<%= file_tree nil %>

docs.title: Building a Prompt Runner
docs.text:
require 'pm'

PM.configure { |c| c.prompts_dir = '~/.prompts' }

# Register project-specific directives
PM.register(:git_diff) { |_ctx| `git diff --cached`.chomp }

# Load and render
system_prompt = PM.parse('agents/code_assistant/system.md')
task_prompt   = PM.parse('agents/code_assistant/review.md')

messages = [
  { role: 'system', content: system_prompt.to_s },
  { role: 'user',   content: task_prompt.to_s(
    'code'     => File.read(ARGV[0]),
    'language' => 'ruby',
    'focus'    => 'security'
  )}
]

# Use metadata for model configuration
model = task_prompt.metadata.model || system_prompt.metadata.model

docs.title: Prompt Versioning
docs.text:
Keep prompts in version control alongside your code. The metadata tracks useful context:

parsed = PM.parse('agents/code_assistant/review.md')

puts parsed.metadata.title        #=> "Code Review Task"
puts parsed.metadata.modified_at  #=> 2025-01-15 10:30:00 -0500

Use modified_at for cache invalidation or audit logging.

docs.title: Parameter Validation Pattern
docs.text:
Check required parameters before rendering:

parsed = PM.parse('agents/code_assistant/review.md')

required = parsed.metadata.parameters
  .select { |_k, v| v.nil? }
  .keys

puts "Required parameters: #{required.join(', ')}"
#=> "Required parameters: code, language"

docs.title: Code Review Prompt
docs.text: A complete example of a parameterized code review prompt.

docs.title: The Prompt File
docs.text:
prompts/code_review.md:

---
title: Code Review
provider: openai
model: gpt-4
temperature: 0.3
parameters:
  language: ruby
  code: null
  style_guide: ~/guides/default.md
---
Review the following <%= language %> code for:
- Correctness
- Performance
- Readability
- Security vulnerabilities

Apply the coding standards from this style guide:
<%= style_guide %>

Code to review:

<%= code %>

docs.title: Parsing
docs.text:
require 'pm'

PM.configure { |c| c.prompts_dir = './prompts' }

parsed = PM.parse('code_review.md')

docs.title: Accessing Metadata
docs.text:
parsed.metadata.title        #=> "Code Review"
parsed.metadata.provider     #=> "openai"
parsed.metadata.model        #=> "gpt-4"
parsed.metadata.temperature  #=> 0.3

parsed.metadata.parameters
#=> {"language" => "ruby", "code" => nil, "style_guide" => "~/guides/default.md"}

Use metadata to configure your LLM client:

client = OpenAI::Client.new
response = client.chat(
  parameters: {
    model:       parsed.metadata.model,
    temperature: parsed.metadata.temperature,
    messages:    [{ role: 'user', content: prompt }]
  }
)

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text:
# Minimal -- supply only the required parameter
prompt = parsed.to_s('code' => File.read('app.rb'))

# Override defaults
prompt = parsed.to_s(
  'code'        => File.read('main.py'),
  'language'    => 'python',
  'style_guide' => File.read('python_style.md')
)

docs.title: Shell Expansion in Action
docs.text:
The style_guide parameter defaults to ~/guides/default.md. If shell expansion is enabled, the ~ is not expanded (it's not a shell variable). But you could use shell references elsewhere in the prompt:

---
title: Code Review with Context
parameters:
  code: null
---
Repository: $(basename $(git rev-parse --toplevel))
Branch: $(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
Reviewer: $USER

Review this code:
<%= code %>

After parsing, the shell references are already resolved:

parsed = PM.parse('code_review_context.md')
parsed.content
#=> "Repository: my-project\nBranch: main\nReviewer: dewayne\n\nReview this code:\n<%= code %>\n"

prompts/common/system_context.md:

---
title: System Context
---
You are a senior software engineer with expertise in <%= language %>.
Current date: $(date +%Y-%m-%d)
User: $USER

prompts/common/output_format.md:

---
title: Output Format
---
Format your response as:
1. Summary (2-3 sentences)
2. Issues found (bulleted list)
3. Suggestions (numbered list)
4. Revised code (if applicable)

prompts/common/ruby_standards.md:

---
title: Ruby Standards
---
Follow these Ruby conventions:
- Use snake_case for methods and variables
- Prefer single-line blocks with braces for short expressions
- Use guard clauses over nested conditionals
- Avoid monkey-patching standard library classes

docs.title: The Composed Prompt
docs.text:
prompts/review.md:

---
title: Full Code Review
parameters:
  language: ruby
  code: null
---
<%= include 'common/system_context.md' %>

<%= include 'common/ruby_standards.md' %>

Review the following code:

<%= code %>

<%= include 'common/output_format.md' %>

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
PM.configure { |c| c.prompts_dir = './prompts' }

parsed = PM.parse('review.md')
prompt = parsed.to_s('code' => File.read('app.rb'))

The rendered prompt combines all four files into a single coherent prompt.

docs.title: Inspecting the Include Tree
docs.text:
parsed.metadata.includes
#=> [
#     { path: ".../common/system_context.md", depth: 1, metadata: {...}, includes: [] },
#     { path: ".../common/ruby_standards.md", depth: 1, metadata: {...}, includes: [] },
#     { path: ".../common/output_format.md",  depth: 1, metadata: {...}, includes: [] }
#   ]

docs.title: Nested Includes
docs.text:
Components can include other components. For example, system_context.md could include a team_info.md:

---
title: System Context
---
You are a senior software engineer.
<%= include 'common/team_info.md' %>

The include tree reflects the nesting:

parsed.metadata.includes[0][:includes]
#=> [{ path: ".../common/team_info.md", depth: 2, metadata: {...}, includes: [] }]

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
• Reuse -- Shared components (system context, output format) written once
  • Consistency -- Changes to a component propagate to all prompts that include it
  • Modularity -- Swap components per use case (different standards for different languages)
  • Traceability -- The includes tree shows exactly what went into each prompt

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
This section covers everything you need to start using PM in your Ruby projects.

  • Installation -- Add PM to your project
  • Quick Start -- Parse your first prompt in a few lines
  • Configuration -- Set global defaults for prompt directories, shell expansion, and ERB rendering

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: PM has three global settings controlled through PM.configure.

docs.title: Setting Defaults
docs.text:
PM.configure do |config|
  config.prompts_dir = '~/.prompts'   # default: ''
  config.shell       = true           # default: true
  config.erb         = true           # default: true
end

docs.title: prompts_dir
docs.text:
Prepended to relative file paths passed to PM.parse. Absolute paths bypass it. Symbols and single words are converted to .md basenames first.

PM.configure { |c| c.prompts_dir = '/usr/share/prompts' }

PM.parse('code_review.md')
#=> reads /usr/share/prompts/code_review.md

PM.parse(:code_review)
#=> reads /usr/share/prompts/code_review.md

PM.parse('code_review')
#=> reads /usr/share/prompts/code_review.md

PM.parse('/absolute/path/review.md')
#=> reads /absolute/path/review.md (prompts_dir ignored)

Subdirectories work naturally:

PM.configure { |c| c.prompts_dir = '~/.prompts' }

PM.parse('agents/summarize.md')
#=> reads ~/.prompts/agents/summarize.md

docs.title: shell
docs.text:
Controls whether shell expansion ($VAR, $(command)) runs during parsing. Defaults to true.

PM.configure { |c| c.shell = false }

# All files now skip shell expansion by default

Per-file YAML metadata overrides the global setting:

---
title: Override Example
shell: true
---
This file gets shell expansion even when the global default is false.
User: $USER

docs.title: erb
docs.text:
Controls whether ERB rendering runs during to_s. Defaults to true.

PM.configure { |c| c.erb = false }

# All files now skip ERB rendering by default

Per-file metadata overrides this too:

---
title: Override Example
erb: true
---
This file renders ERB even when the global default is false.
Result: <%= 2 + 2 %>

docs.title: Resetting
docs.text:
Restore all settings to their defaults:

PM.config.reset!

PM.config.prompts_dir  #=> ''
PM.config.shell        #=> true
PM.config.erb          #=> true

docs.title: Accessing Current Settings
docs.text:
PM.config.prompts_dir
PM.config.shell
PM.config.erb

PM.config returns the singleton PM::Configuration instance. PM.configure yields the same instance.

docs.title: Gemfile
docs.text:
Add PM to your Gemfile:

gem 'prompt_manager'

Then run:

bundle install

docs.title: Manual Install
docs.text: gem install prompt_manager

docs.title: Require
docs.text:
require 'pm'

The PM module is the primary interface. All public methods are accessed through it.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Ruby >= 3.2.0
  • No runtime dependencies beyond the standard library (plus ostruct on Ruby 4.0+)

docs.title: Parse a String
docs.text:
require 'pm'

parsed = PM.parse("---\ntitle: Hello\n---\nContent here")

parsed.metadata.title  #=> "Hello"
parsed.content         #=> "\nContent here\n"

docs.title: Parse a File
docs.text:
Given greeting.md:

---
title: Greeting
parameters:
  name: null
---
Hello, <%= name %>! Welcome.

# Any of these forms work:
parsed = PM.parse('greeting.md')    # explicit .md extension
parsed = PM.parse(:greeting)        # Symbol — .md appended
parsed = PM.parse('greeting')       # single word — .md appended

parsed.metadata.title       #=> "Greeting"
parsed.metadata.parameters  #=> {"name" => nil}

# Render with parameters
puts parsed.to_s('name' => 'Alice')
#=> "Hello, Alice! Welcome."

When parsing a file, PM also adds directory, name, created_at, and modified_at to the metadata.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameters declared in the YAML front-matter define template variables:

  • null value -- parameter is required; to_s raises ArgumentError if missing
  • Any other value -- used as the default; can be overridden in to_s
parsed = PM.parse("---\nparameters:\n  lang: ruby\n  code: null\n---\n<%= lang %>: <%= code %>")

# Use defaults where available, supply required params
parsed.to_s('code' => 'puts "hi"')  #=> "ruby: puts \"hi\""

# Override defaults
parsed.to_s('code' => 'print("hi")', 'lang' => 'python')

docs.title: Shell Expansion
docs.text:
Environment variables and commands are expanded at parse time:

---
title: Info
---
User: $USER
Date: $(date +%Y-%m-%d)

parsed = PM.parse('info.md')
parsed.content  #=> "User: dewayne\nDate: 2025-01-15\n"

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Configuration -- Set a prompts directory and global defaults
  • Parsing Guide -- File vs string parsing in depth
  • Parameters Guide -- Required and default parameters

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
In-depth guides for each PM feature.

  • Parsing Prompts -- File paths vs raw strings, metadata extraction
  • Parameters -- Required and default parameters, rendering with to_s
  • Shell Expansion -- Environment variables and command substitution
  • ERB Rendering -- Template evaluation and disabling
  • Including Files -- Composing prompts from multiple files
  • Custom Directives -- Registering your own ERB helpers
  • Comment Stripping -- HTML comment removal

docs.title: Comment Stripping
docs.text: HTML comments are stripped before any other processing stage.

docs.title: Automatic Stripping
docs.text:
Comments are removed during PM.parse:

<!-- This comment will be removed -->
---
title: My Prompt
---
Content here. <!-- This too -->

After parsing:

parsed = PM.parse(source)
parsed.content  #=> "\nContent here. \n"

docs.title: Multiline Comments
docs.text:
Multiline comments are fully removed:

<!--
This entire block
is removed
-->
---
title: Example
---
Visible content.

docs.title: Comments Before Metadata
docs.text:
Comments before the YAML front-matter are stripped first, so the metadata parser sees clean input:

<!-- Editor note: draft version -->
---
title: My Prompt
---
Content

docs.title: Direct Access
docs.text:
The comment stripping method is available as a standalone utility:

PM.strip_comments("Hello <!-- removed --> World")
#=> "Hello  World"

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Editor notes -- Leave comments for prompt authors that don't appear in the rendered output
  • Disabled sections -- Temporarily comment out parts of a prompt
  • Documentation -- Annotate prompt files without affecting the AI input

docs.title: Custom Directives
docs.text: Register custom methods that become available inside ERB templates.

docs.title: Registering a Directive
docs.text:
PM.register(:read) { |_ctx, path| File.read(path) }
PM.register(:env)  { |_ctx, key| ENV.fetch(key, '') }
PM.register(:run)  { |_ctx, cmd| `#{cmd}`.chomp }

Use them in any prompt file:

---
title: Deploy Prompt
---
Hostname: <%= read '/etc/hostname' %>
Environment: <%= env 'DEPLOY_ENV' %>
Recent commits: <%= run 'git log --oneline -5' %>

docs.title: Aliases
docs.text:
Register multiple names for the same directive by passing additional names:

PM.register(:webpage, :website, :web) { |_ctx, url| fetch_page(url) }

All names point to the same block. Use any of them in ERB:

<%= webpage 'https://example.com' %>
<%= web 'https://example.com' %>

Duplicate detection still applies — if any name is already registered, an error is raised.

docs.title: The RenderContext
docs.text:
The first argument to every directive block is a PM::RenderContext with access to the current render state:

Field Type Description directory String Directory of the file being rendered params Hash Merged parameter values metadata PM::Metadata Current file's metadata depth Integer Include nesting depth (0 for top-level) included Set File paths already in the include chain 
PM.register(:current_file) { |ctx| ctx.metadata.name || 'unknown' }
PM.register(:nesting) { |ctx| ctx.depth.to_s }

The context is always the first argument. Additional arguments come from the ERB call:

PM.register(:greet) { |_ctx, name| "Hello, #{name}!" }

<%= greet 'Alice' %>

docs.title: Duplicate Registration
docs.text:
Registering a name that already exists raises an error:

PM.register(:include) { |_ctx, path| path }
#=> RuntimeError: Directive already registered: include

This protects built-in directives from being overwritten.

docs.title: Resetting Directives
docs.text:
Remove all custom directives and restore only the built-ins:

PM.reset_directives!

After reset, only the built-in directives are registered: include, insert, and read.

docs.title: Directives in Included Files
docs.text:
Custom directives are available in included files too. They share the same directive registry:

<!-- parent.md -->
<%= include 'child.md' %>

<!-- child.md -->
<%= read '/etc/hostname' %>

docs.title: Name Format
docs.text:
Both symbols and strings are accepted:

PM.register(:my_helper) { |_ctx| "works" }
PM.register('other_helper') { |_ctx| "also works" }

docs.title: Class-Based Directives
docs.text:
For organized groups of directives, subclass PM::Directive:

class MyDirectives < PM::Directive
  desc "Fetch environment variable"
  def env(ctx, key)
    ENV.fetch(key, '')
  end

  desc "Run a shell command"
  def run(ctx, cmd)
    `#{cmd}`.chomp
  end
  alias_method :exec, :run

  # No desc — not registered as a directive
  def helper
    "internal"
  end
end

PM::Directive.register_all

desc marks the next method as a directive. Methods without desc are ordinary helpers and won't be registered. alias_method aliases are detected automatically via UnboundMethod#original_name.

docs.title: Category name
docs.text:
The class name determines a category heading (useful for help output):

MyDirectives.category_name  #=> "My"
PM::CoreDirectives.category_name  #=> "Core"

The last segment of the class name is used, with Directives stripped and camelCase split.

docs.title: Dispatch customization
docs.text:
Override build_dispatch_block to customize how methods are called when dispatched through PM.directives:

class MyDirectives < PM::Directive
  class << self
    # Default: proc { |ctx, *args| inst.send(method_name, ctx, *args) }
    def build_dispatch_block(inst, method_name)
      proc { |_ctx, *args| inst.send(method_name, args.flatten) }
    end
  end
end

docs.title: Subclass tracking
docs.text:
All PM::Directive subclasses (direct and indirect) are tracked centrally:

PM::Directive.directive_subclasses
#=> [PM::CoreDirectives, MyDirectives, ...]

register_all iterates this list, creates a singleton instance per subclass, and registers each described method with PM.register.

docs.title: Listing Directives
docs.text:
PM.directives
#=> { include: #<Proc>, insert: #<Proc>, read: #<Proc>, ... }

docs.title: ERB Rendering
docs.text: ERB templates are evaluated on demand when to_s is called.

docs.title: Basics
docs.text:
Any <%= expression %> in the content is evaluated as Ruby:

---
title: Math
---
Result: <%= 2 + 2 %>
Today: <%= Time.now.strftime('%Y-%m-%d') %>

parsed = PM.parse('math.md')
parsed.to_s  #=> "Result: 4\nToday: 2025-01-15\n"

docs.title: Template Parameters
docs.text:
Parameters declared in the YAML front-matter are available as local methods inside ERB:

---
title: Greeting
parameters:
  name: World
---
Hello, <%= name %>!

parsed = PM.parse('greeting.md')
parsed.to_s                    #=> "Hello, World!"
parsed.to_s('name' => 'Alice') #=> "Hello, Alice!"

See Parameters for details on required vs default values.

docs.title: Registered Directives
docs.text:
Custom directives registered with PM.register are also available in ERB:

PM.register(:upcase) { |_ctx, str| str.upcase }

---
title: Example
---
<%= upcase 'hello' %>

See Custom Directives for the full guide.

docs.title: Built-in Directives
docs.text:
PM includes one built-in directive:

  • include -- Include and render another prompt file. See Including Files.

docs.title: Disabling ERB
docs.text:
Set erb: false in the file's YAML metadata:

---
title: Raw Template
erb: false
---
This <%= expression %> is preserved as-is.

When ERB is disabled:

  • to_s returns the content without template evaluation
  • Parameters are ignored
  • The include directive does not execute
  • metadata.includes is an empty array after to_s

docs.title: Global Default
docs.text:
PM.configure { |c| c.erb = false }

Per-file metadata always overrides the global setting. A file with erb: true gets ERB rendering even when the global default is false.

docs.title: Pipeline Position
docs.text:
ERB rendering is the last stage of the pipeline, executed on demand:

  1. Strip HTML comments
  2. Extract YAML metadata
  3. Shell expansion (at parse time)
  4. ERB rendering (at to_s time)

This means shell variables are already expanded before ERB sees the content. If content contains both $VAR and <%= param %>, the shell variable is resolved first, then ERB fills in the parameters.

docs.title: Including Files
docs.text: The include directive lets you compose prompts from multiple files.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
---
title: Full Review
parameters:
  code: null
---
<%= include 'common/header.md' %>

Review this code:
<%= code %>

<%= include 'common/footer.md' %>

parsed = PM.parse('full_review.md')
puts parsed.to_s('code' => File.read('app.rb'))

docs.title: How Includes Work
docs.text:
Each included file goes through the full processing pipeline:

  1. HTML comments stripped
  2. YAML metadata extracted
  3. Shell expansion applied
  4. ERB rendered (with the parent's parameter values)

The included file's rendered content replaces the <%= include ... %> tag.

docs.title: Path Resolution
docs.text:
Include paths are resolved relative to the parent file's directory:

prompts/
  review.md          # contains: <%= include 'common/header.md' %>
  common/
    header.md        # resolved from prompts/common/header.md

docs.title: Parameter Passing
docs.text:
The parent's parameter values are passed to included files. Child files can use the same parameter names:

<!-- parent.md -->
---
parameters:
  name: null
---
<%= include 'greeting.md' %>
Done.

<!-- greeting.md -->
---
title: Greeting
---
Hello, <%= name %>!

parsed = PM.parse('parent.md')
parsed.to_s('name' => 'Alice')
#=> "Hello, Alice!\nDone."

docs.title: Nested Includes
docs.text:
Includes can be nested. File A can include File B, which includes File C:

<!-- a.md -->
<%= include 'b.md' %>

<!-- b.md -->
<%= include 'c.md' %>

<!-- c.md -->
Content from C

docs.title: Circular Include Detection
docs.text:
PM detects circular includes and raises an error:

<!-- circular_a.md -->
<%= include 'circular_b.md' %>

<!-- circular_b.md -->
<%= include 'circular_a.md' %>

PM.parse('circular_a.md').to_s
#=> RuntimeError: Circular include detected: /path/to/circular_a.md

docs.title: Includes Metadata
docs.text:
After calling to_s, the parent's metadata has an includes key with a tree of what was included:

parsed = PM.parse('full_review.md')
parsed.to_s('code' => source)

parsed.metadata.includes
#=> [
#     {
#       path:     "/prompts/common/header.md",
#       depth:    1,
#       metadata: { title: "Header", ... },
#       includes: []
#     },
#     {
#       path:     "/prompts/common/footer.md",
#       depth:    1,
#       metadata: { title: "Footer", ... },
#       includes: []
#     }
#   ]

Nested includes form a tree -- each entry's includes array contains its own children.

The includes array is nil before to_s is called and is reset on each call.

docs.title: insert / read — Raw File Insertion
docs.text:
Use insert (or its alias read) to insert a file's content verbatim. Unlike include, the content is not parsed, shell-expanded, or ERB-rendered:

---
title: Code Review
---
Review this code:

```ruby
<%= insert 'src/app.rb' %>

### Differences from `include`

| | `insert` | `include` |
|---|---|---|
| File types | Any | `.md` only |
| ERB in content | Preserved as literal text | Rendered |
| Shell expansion | Not applied | Applied |
| Recursion | None | Nested includes supported |
| Metadata tracking | None | `metadata.includes` tree |

### Path resolution

Same as `include` — paths resolve relative to the parent file's directory. Absolute paths work from any context, including string-parsed prompts.

### Missing files

Raises an error:

```ruby
PM.parse("---\n---\n<%= insert '/no/such/file' %>").to_s
#=> RuntimeError: insert: file not found: /no/such/file

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• The include directive requires file context. Using it with string-parsed prompts raises an error:
PM.parse("---\n---\n<%= include 'other.md' %>").to_s
#=> RuntimeError: include requires a file context (use PM.parse with a file path)
  • When erb: false, the include directive does not execute and metadata.includes is an empty array.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameters are declared in the YAML parameters hash and used as ERB template variables.

docs.title: Declaring Parameters
docs.text:
---
title: Code Review
parameters:
  language: ruby
  code: null
  style_guide: ~/guides/default.md
---
Review the following <%= language %> code using the style guide
at <%= style_guide %>:

<%= code %>

docs.title: Required vs Default
docs.text:
• null value -- the parameter is required. to_s raises ArgumentError if not provided.
  • Any other value -- used as the default. Can be overridden when calling to_s.
parsed = PM.parse('code_review.md')

parsed.metadata.parameters
#=> {"language" => "ruby", "code" => nil, "style_guide" => "~/guides/default.md"}

docs.title: Rendering with to_s
docs.text:
to_s accepts a Hash of parameter values:

# Supply required params, accept defaults for the rest
parsed.to_s('code' => File.read('app.rb'))

# Override a default
parsed.to_s('code' => File.read('app.py'), 'language' => 'python')

Symbol keys work too:

parsed.to_s(code: File.read('app.rb'))

docs.title: All Defaults
docs.text:
When every parameter has a default value, to_s needs no arguments:

parsed.to_s  #=> renders with all defaults

docs.title: Missing Required Parameters
docs.text:
Calling to_s without supplying a required parameter raises ArgumentError:

parsed.to_s
#=> ArgumentError: Missing required parameters: code

The error message lists all missing parameters.

docs.title: Parameters in Included Files
docs.text:
When a file includes another file via <%= include 'child.md' %>, the parent's parameter values are passed to the child. The child can use the same parameter names:

<!-- parent.md -->
---
title: Parent
parameters:
  name: null
---
<%= include 'greeting.md' %>

<!-- greeting.md -->
---
title: Greeting
---
Hello, <%= name %>!

parsed = PM.parse('parent.md')
parsed.to_s('name' => 'Alice')
#=> "Hello, Alice!"

docs.title: Parsing Prompts
docs.text: PM.parse is the main entry point. It accepts a file path, a Symbol, a single word, or a raw string.

docs.title: File Paths
docs.text:
A source is treated as a file path when it:

  • Is a Pathname object
  • Responds to to_path
  • Is a String ending in .md
  • Is a Symbol (.md is appended, e.g. :code_review → code_review.md)
  • Is a single word containing only letters, digits, or underscores (.md is appended, e.g. "code_review" → code_review.md)
# String file path
parsed = PM.parse('code_review.md')

# Pathname
parsed = PM.parse(Pathname.new('code_review.md'))

# Symbol (basename — .md appended)
parsed = PM.parse(:code_review)

# Single word (basename — .md appended)
parsed = PM.parse('code_review')

When parsing a file, PM adds these keys to the metadata automatically:

Key Type Description directory String Absolute path to the file's parent directory name String Filename (e.g., code_review.md) created_at Time File creation timestamp modified_at Time Last modification timestamp

docs.title: prompts_dir
docs.text:
Relative file paths are resolved against PM.config.prompts_dir:

PM.configure { |c| c.prompts_dir = '~/.prompts' }

PM.parse('agents/summarize.md')
#=> reads ~/.prompts/agents/summarize.md

Absolute paths bypass prompts_dir:

PM.parse('/etc/prompts/system.md')
#=> reads /etc/prompts/system.md regardless of prompts_dir

docs.title: Raw Strings
docs.text:
Any other string is parsed directly:

parsed = PM.parse("---
title: Hello
---
Content here")

parsed.metadata.title  #=> "Hello"
parsed.content         #=> "
Content here
"

String-parsed prompts do not have directory, name, created_at, or modified_at in their metadata.

Include limitations

The include directive requires file context to resolve relative paths. It raises an error when used with string-parsed prompts.

docs.title: Metadata Extraction
docs.text:
YAML front-matter is delimited by --- fences:

---
title: My Prompt
provider: openai
model: gpt-4
temperature: 0.3
---
The prompt content starts here.

All YAML keys become accessible via dot notation on the PM::Metadata object:

parsed.metadata.title        #=> "My Prompt"
parsed.metadata.provider     #=> "openai"
parsed.metadata.temperature  #=> 0.3

Boolean keys also get predicate methods:

parsed.metadata.shell   #=> true
parsed.metadata.shell?  #=> true

docs.title: No Metadata
docs.text:
Files without front-matter are valid. The metadata object is empty and the entire content is preserved:

parsed = PM.parse("Just plain text")
parsed.metadata.title  #=> nil
parsed.content         #=> "Just plain text"

docs.title: Bracket Accessor
docs.text:
You can also access metadata with bracket notation:

parsed[:title]  #=> "My Prompt"

docs.title: Pipeline Stages
docs.text:
After parsing, the content has been through these stages:

  1. HTML comments stripped
  2. YAML metadata extracted
  3. Shell expansion applied (if shell: true)

ERB rendering happens later, on demand, when to_s is called.

docs.title: Shell Expansion
docs.text: Shell expansion replaces environment variable references and command substitutions with their values at parse time.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: Pattern Description Example $VAR Environment variable $USER ${VAR} Environment variable (braced) ${HOME} $(command) Command substitution $(date +%Y-%m-%d)

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
---
title: Info
---
Current user: $USER
Home directory: ${HOME}

After parsing:

parsed = PM.parse('info.md')
parsed.content
#=> "Current user: dewayne\nHome directory: /Users/dewayne\n"

Only UPPERCASE variable names are expanded. Lowercase names like $foo are left as-is.

Missing environment variables are replaced with an empty string.

docs.title: Command Substitution
docs.text:
---
title: Context
---
Date: $(date +%Y-%m-%d)
Branch: $(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)

Commands are executed via the shell and replaced with their stdout (trailing newline stripped).

docs.title: Nested Commands
docs.text:
Nested parentheses are handled correctly:

$(echo $(echo hello))

docs.title: Failed Commands
docs.text:
A command that exits with a non-zero status raises RuntimeError:

PM.parse("Output: $(exit 1)")
#=> RuntimeError: Command failed with exit status 1: exit 1

docs.title: Direct Access
docs.text:
Shell expansion is available as a standalone method:

PM.expand_shell("Hello $USER from $(hostname)")
#=> "Hello dewayne from venus"

docs.title: Disabling Shell Expansion
docs.text:
Set shell: false in the file's YAML metadata:

---
title: Raw
shell: false
---
This $USER reference is preserved as-is.

Or disable globally:

PM.configure { |c| c.shell = false }

Per-file metadata always overrides the global setting. A file with shell: true gets shell expansion even when the global default is false.

docs.title: Interaction with ERB
docs.text:
Shell expansion happens at parse time (step 3 of the pipeline). ERB rendering happens later when to_s is called (step 4). This means shell references in the raw template are expanded before ERB sees the content.

If you need dynamic shell output at render time, use a custom directive instead:

PM.register(:sh) { |_ctx, cmd| `#{cmd}`.chomp }
